newsitem.title: POLAND: Espebepe plans issue if debt-deal passed.
newsitem.headline: Espebepe plans issue if debt-deal passed.

text.p: Polish ailing construction firm Espebepe plans a new issue for its creditors of 20 percent of current share capital priced at five zlotys per share if they agree to a debt write-off deal, Espebepe's president said.
Andrzej Hass told a news conference on Tuesday some shareholders had already agreed to the proposal.
"If the debt write-off deal is accepted I will immediately ask the supervisory board to call a shareholders' meeting to vote on the issue -- it will have to be quick," he said.
The next creditors' meeting is scheduled for May 16, after two previous ones on March 14 and April 14 failed to decide on the fate of the company.

Espebepe, with debts of 75 million zlotys, seeks a write-off of 95 percent from its largest creditors. The firm had a net loss of 52.1 million zlotys in 1996 and 2.6 million in the first quarter of 1997 and has 2.15 million shares.
Hass also said that if the debt write-off deal was accepted the company could show profit by 1999.
"In 1999 we should conclude the process of the firm's restructuring and show profit," he said.

He added that if the debt write-off was accepted the written-off debts would show as extraordinary profit in the company's books, boosting its net to 50 million zlotys in 1997. It would still show operating losses in 1997 and 1998.

Lucyna Fila of consulting firm Nicom Consulting Ltd advising Espebepe in its restructuring process, also present, said that after the new issue, the net asset value per share would be 7.9 zlotys in 1997.
Earnings per share would be 20.3 zlotys in 1997, she said.
Hass said that the May 16 creditors' meeting would be the last and if creditors did not agree to the debt reduction deal the firm would have to file for bankruptcy.

He added that the firm was negotiating the debt write-off and the new issue proposal with its creditors, including the biggest Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS), and was ready to make adjustments to the offer if they were needed.

He said, however, that the previous proposal of PBKS envisaging a 40-percent debt write-off and an issue of convertible bonds for the remaining debt was unacceptable because it was too time-consuming and too expensive.
If the plan failed, Espebepe could become the first bankruptcy on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since it was restored in 1991.
